citation: Dewald, J. F., Meijer, A. M., Oort, F. J., Kerkhof, G. A., & Bögels, S. M. (2010). The influence of sleep quality, sleep duration and sleepiness on school performance in children and adolescents: A meta-analytic review. Sleep Medicine Reviews, 14(3), 179–189. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.smrv.2009.10.004
use: Meta-analysis of distinct sleep measures and school performance. Its pooled sleep-duration correlation was modest (r = .069), much smaller than the deliberately constructed exemplar's r = .7472.
boundary: The pooled estimate combines heterogeneous published studies and cannot substantiate the fictional class's correlation or imply a causal effect.

citation: Curcio, G., Ferrara, M., & De Gennaro, L. (2006). Sleep loss, learning capacity and academic performance. Sleep Medicine Reviews, 10(5), 323–337. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.smrv.2005.11.001
use: Review of sleep loss, learning and academic performance across observational and manipulated-sleep research, providing contextual rather than sample-specific evidence.
boundary: Designs and outcomes in this review differ from the invented single-quiz observational dataset. It does not verify the exemplar's effect size, survey procedure or causal mechanism.
